page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 2-core AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this arm64 server features 4.0 GB of memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1473.0. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show limitations, as evidenced by a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 3041.67 and a poor Passmark memory score of 1082.76. Large-block read memory bandwidth is average at 53.57 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is weaker at 20.54 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gd.large offers a dense compute profile with high-speed local storage on an energy-efficient ARM architecture, though it trades off multi-threaded performance and memory capacity. This hardware configuration is suited for single-threaded workloads, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and applications requiring fast local scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.large is a compute-optimized, arm64-based instance featuring a dedicated 2.6 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, operating on the Nitro hypervisor with a 1 Gbps baseline network speed. Benchmark data shows average single-core performance, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1473.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.88, though multi-core and memory-write metrics are weaker. Qualitatively, this instance provides a cost-efficient entry point for ARM-based compute workloads that benefit from high-speed local storage but do not require extensive memory or multi-threaded scaling. It is suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded applications, and basic text processing.
